answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent locks a bond before it can earn, and its earning rate rises only with verified work over time, then fades without it. A sybil attacker must split the bond across thousands of fake identities, each too weak to earn much, while keeping them all active costs more than they return - like a gale tearing at a velvet curtain, no single thread holds. An honest agent's steady record instead compounds into something like a sonnet: simple lines, hard to fake, cheap to check.
